title: Influence from the thresholded derivative
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ map the $n$-dimensional sign cube $\\{\pm1\}^n$ to $\{\pm1\}$, and let $p:\{\pm1\}^n\to\bbr$ satisfy $f(x)=1$ when $p(x)\ge 0$ and $f(x)=-1$ when $p(x)<0$, with $p(x)\ne 0$ for every $x$. For any coordinate $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the uniform average of $f(x)x_i$ times the threshold sign of the discrete derivative $D_i p(x)$ equals the influence $\mathbb{E}_x[(D_i f(x))^2]$, where $D_i g(x)=(g(x^{i,+})-g(x^{i,-}))/2$, and $x^{i,+}$ and $x^{i,-}$ are obtained by setting coordinate $i$ to $+1$ and $-1$, respectively; the threshold sign is $+1$ when its argument is zero.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the $n$-dimensional sign cube to signs
$p$ is real-valued on the sign cube
$i$ is a coordinate in the $n$-dimensional cube
